title: Crit Racing on 40 mm Tires – GR:ONE Road Build (Part 1)

takeaways.text: A 52T aero 1× chainring fitted with no spacer hack: a 3 mm hex key still passed between ring and chainstay, and the gap looked large enough for bigger rings.
Built as a crit bike with 40 mm tires, aero bottles and Look Keo pedals, it weighed about 7.6 kg, slightly lighter than the owner's road bike.

Despite 7 mm more listed bottom-bracket drop than his Winspace road bike, pedal clearance on 40 mm tires measured slightly higher; the 2° slacker head angle and longer wheelbase make it less nimble and need more counter-steering.
In a 90-rider beginner crit (45 km/h average, 52 km/h fastest lap) the 40 mm setup at 40 psi felt grippy and fast, not squishy, and the handling never bothered him.

disclosure: The creator converts his own GR:ONE into a road race setup; the description mentions no sponsorship for the frame.
summary: The owner rebuilds his GR:ONE as a road race bike with deep wheels, 40 mm tires and a 52T ring and races a local crit to test whether an aero gravel frame can double as a road bike.
